draft.title: Fractional distillation of crude oil
card: Crude oil is a mixture of many hydrocarbons. Fractional distillation separates it into parts called fractions, using the fact that each hydrocarbon has a different boiling point.
The oil is heated until most of it is vapour. The vapour enters the bottom of a tall column, which is hot at the bottom and cooler towards the top.
As the vapour rises, each part cools until it reaches its boiling point. There it condenses back to a liquid and is drawn off.

Small molecules have low boiling points and collect near the top. These include petrol. Large molecules have high boiling points and collect near the bottom. These include bitumen. Diesel sits between them.
draft.remember: The column is hot at the bottom and cool at the top. Each fraction condenses where the temperature falls to its boiling point.

a.q: Why do the parts of crude oil separate as vapour rises up the column?
opts: Each part condenses at a different temperature
Each part has a different colour and floats
Each part burns at a different height
Each part dissolves in the cooler liquid
a.why: Each hydrocarbon has its own boiling point, so each condenses where the column has cooled to that temperature. Colour does not decide where a part is collected.
a.clue: Think about boiling points and the changing temperature of the column.

b.q: A refinery in Geelong separates crude oil. Fraction X is drawn off near the top of the column. Fraction Y is drawn off near the bottom. Which statement is correct?
opts: X has a lower boiling point than Y
X has a higher boiling point than Y
X has larger molecules than Y
X was heated more than Y
b.why: Vapour that rises near the top only condenses where it is cool, so it has a low boiling point and small molecules. Fraction Y condenses where it is hot, so its molecules are larger and its boiling point is higher.
b.clue: Which fraction stays as a vapour the longest as it rises?

wants.brief: A tall fractionating column with a furnace feeding hot crude oil vapour in at the bottom. The column is labelled hot at the bottom and cool at the top. Fractions are drawn off at levels, labelled from top to bottom: petrol, diesel, bitumen. Add arrows for rising vapour.
wants.why: It shows how temperature changes up the column and where each fraction is collected.

a.best: Each part condenses at a different temperature

b.best: X has a lower boiling point than Y
